title: CWCOT Program — Claims Without Conveyance of Title Requirements
content:
Claims Without Conveyance of Title (CWCOT) Program Policy — CTL Requirements for CWCOT-Eligible Properties.

Background: The CWCOT program is an alternative claims process established by HUD for FHA-insured mortgages. Under the traditional process, a servicer forecloses, conveys the property to HUD, and HUD disposes of the property as part of its REO inventory. Under CWCOT, the servicer is authorized to sell the property at foreclosure sale or through a post-foreclosure auction without conveying to HUD. The servicer files a claim for the difference between the sale proceeds and the outstanding mortgage balance. This program is governed by HUD Mortgagee Letter 2016-16 and subsequent updates. HUD Mortgagee Letter 2022-09 updated the Commissioner-Adjusted Fair Market Value methodology.

Section 1 — Eligibility Criteria:
A property qualifies for CWCOT disposition when: (a) the underlying mortgage is FHA-insured, (b) the property has been through a completed foreclosure sale with no redemption period remaining or redemption period has expired, (c) the servicer has obtained an FHA appraisal establishing the as-is value, and (d) the property is not subject to an active bankruptcy stay. If any eligibility criterion is not met, the property must follow the standard conveyance path.

Section 2 — Appraisal Requirements:
All CWCOT properties require an FHA appraisal performed by a HUD-approved appraiser. The appraisal must reflect the as-is condition of the property. The Commissioner-Adjusted Fair Market Value is calculated by HUD based on the appraised value and local market conditions. The initial sale price at foreclosure auction must be set at or above the Commissioner-Adjusted Fair Market Value. If the property does not sell at foreclosure auction at or above this value, a second-chance sale may be conducted at a reduced price, typically set at a percentage of the appraised value as determined by HUD schedules.

Section 3 — Property Condition Requirements:
Before marketing a CWCOT property, the servicer must ensure minimum property condition standards are met. The property must be secured against unauthorized entry. All utilities must be verified as functional or properly winterized. Hazardous conditions including mold contamination, structural damage posing safety risks, and environmental hazards must be identified in the appraisal. Properties with health and safety issues may still be marketed under CWCOT with appropriate buyer disclosure and as-is sale terms.

Section 4 — Timeline Requirements:
HUD prescribes maximum timelines for servicer action. First legal action for foreclosure must be initiated within the timeframe specified by HUD for the applicable state (typically within six months of default for non-judicial foreclosure states and within applicable timelines for judicial foreclosure states). Post-foreclosure, the servicer must initiate marketing within 30 days. If the property does not sell at initial foreclosure auction, the second-chance auction must be listed within 15 days. Total elapsed time from default to final disposition is monitored by HUD and excessive delays may result in curtailment of the insurance claim.

Section 5 — CTL Determination for CWCOT:
When performing CTL determination on a CWCOT property, the following additional checks apply beyond the baseline CTL requirements: (a) verify FHA case number is active and in good standing, (b) confirm appraisal is current and not stale (CWCOT appraisals are valid for 120 days from effective date), (c) verify Commissioner-Adjusted Fair Market Value has been received from HUD, (d) confirm property preservation requirements have been met per HUD guidelines, and (e) verify no open HUD compliance findings exist on the case.

Section 6 — Second-Chance Sale:
If a property did not sell at the initial foreclosure auction, the servicer may conduct a second-chance sale at a reduced price. The second-chance minimum bid is typically calculated as a percentage of the appraised value. Properties in the second-chance phase have already cleared initial CTL requirements but must be re-verified for occupancy status and property condition before relisting. A new field inspection is required if more than 30 days have elapsed since the previous inspection.

References: HUD Mortgagee Letter 2016-16 (CWCOT program establishment), HUD Mortgagee Letter 2022-09 (Commissioner-Adjusted Fair Market Value updates), 24 CFR Part 203 (FHA single-family mortgage insurance), HUD Handbook 4000.1 (FHA Single Family Housing Policy Handbook).
